saml.description: Keycloak does not validate the Issuer of received SAML assertions when the SAML identity provider configuration leaves Identity Provider Entity ID empty.
saml.note: A successful login with a mismatched Issuer is by design in this configuration and should not be flagged unless issuer validation was configured.

saml.description: Brokered usernames may be lower-cased unless case-sensitive username is enabled on the identity provider.
saml.note: Case-only differences between sent and granted identity can be expected normalization rather than identity collapse.

saml.description: The first broker login flow may link to an existing local account with the same email or username depending on configured authenticators.
saml.note: Account linking during first broker login is configurable behavior and must be distinguished from unintended principal collapse.

saml.description: When Trust Email is enabled, brokered email addresses are treated as verified and may be updated on subsequent logins depending on sync mode.
saml.note: Email-verified state changes are by design and affect account-linking interpretations.

saml.description: Default first broker login flow can automatically create a new local user when no matching account exists.
saml.note: Creation of a new account on first broker login is normal and not an identity confusion bug.

saml.description: Automatically linking existing users without prompting is a documented but dangerous configuration choice.
saml.note: Account linking collisions under an intentionally unsafe AutoLink-style flow are admin-chosen behavior, not necessarily a product defect.

saml.description: When SAML step-up authentication is not enabled or not fully configured, Keycloak continues and returns the legacy unspecified AuthnContextClassRef instead of erroring.
saml.note: Absence of step-up enforcement can be backward-compatible behavior rather than an authorization bug.

saml.description: After successful identity provider login, the browser authentication flow does not continue; extra steps such as MFA require a configured post login flow.
saml.note: A brokered login bypassing MFA configured only in the browser flow is expected unless a post login flow enforces MFA.

saml.description: When SAML step-up authentication is not enabled or not fully configured, Keycloak continues and returns AuthnContextClassRef 'unspecified' instead of erroring.
saml.note: Missing requested AuthnContext enforcement may be backward-compatibility behavior unless the step-up feature and mappings are configured.

saml.constraint: For SAML issuer-validation tests (I1 saml_issuer_mismatch), create_provider MUST set Identity Provider Entity ID via config.idpEntityId. If this field is empty, Keycloak performs no Issuer validation on received SAML assertions.

For insecure-default signature-validation tests (I1 saml_cert_substitution), create_provider with default SAML settings may not validate signatures unless config.validateSignature is enabled and assertion-signing expectations are configured. A login succeeding with default config is only meaningful when validateSignature and wantAssertionsSigned were intentionally left unset to test defaults.

For assertion-integrity tests (I1 saml_unsigned_assertion, saml_spurious_signature, saml_post_binding_unsigned_assertion), create_provider SHOULD set config.wantAssertionsSigned=true. Otherwise Keycloak may accept a signed response envelope without requiring an individually signed assertion by configuration, causing false positives about proof-integrity enforcement.

For signature-validation tests against static certs, create_provider MUST set config.useMetadataDescriptorUrl=false and provide config.signingCertificate. If useMetadataDescriptorUrl is true, Keycloak refreshes validating certificates from metadata and test trust anchors may change due to cache refresh behavior.

For signature-validation tests against metadata, create_provider MUST set config.useMetadataDescriptorUrl=true and config.metadataDescriptorUrl to the intended metadata source. Keycloak caches certificates and may refresh automatically depending on binding and metadata cacheDuration/validUntil, so trust-anchor changes may not take effect immediately.

For I2 replay tests, SAML assertions are stateful and should not be treated like stateless JWT bearer assertions. Use TWO saml_login events with the same fixed_assertion_id to test assertion ID replay, and with include_onetimeuse=true plus the same fixed_assertion_id to test OneTimeUse replay.

For I2 expired-assertion tests, include a CONTROL saml_login without expired_assertion=true before the attack login. Without a control, a failed expired assertion login cannot be distinguished from broken SAML provider setup.

For I5 audience/conditions tests, use saml_login with remove_conditions=true to test missing Conditions. If login succeeds, Keycloak accepted an assertion with no temporal or audience constraints. A separate wrong-audience test must include a Conditions element with an AudienceRestriction targeting a different SP entity ID.

Principal selection for SAML brokered identities is controlled by config.principalType and config.principalAttribute. For I4 identity-collision tests, the fuzzer MUST know whether Keycloak binds identities by Subject NameID or by a SAML attribute. Testing email-binding collision is only valid when principalType is configured to use an email-bearing attribute rather than Subject NameID.

NameID transient format cannot be combined with Subject NameID principal type. If create_provider sets config.nameIDPolicyFormat to urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:nameid-format:transient, do NOT configure principalType to Subject NameID; this is an invalid setup and will confound I4 tests.

The general identity-provider setting 'Essential claim value' supports regular expression matching. For multi-identity I4 tests, do not assume exact matching if this filter is enabled; either omit the essential-claim filter or intentionally configure a regex that matches all intended identities.

Case-sensitive username behavior is configurable on identity providers. If case-sensitive username is disabled, brokered usernames are lower-cased before federation. I4 case-confusion tests must account for this by-design normalization and should not flag Admin vs admin collapse as a vulnerability when this setting is off.

Trust Email causes brokered email addresses to be treated as verified, and with sync mode FORCE this verified state can be updated on subsequent logins. For I4 unverified-email-account-linking tests, create_provider MUST keep trustEmail=false; otherwise email-based linking/verification behavior is intentionally broadened by configuration.

First Login Flow determines whether existing local accounts are linked, created, or require re-authentication/email verification. I4 account-linking tests MUST control firstBrokerLoginFlowAlias explicitly. Using the dangerous automatic-link flow can intentionally link accounts by email/username and would otherwise look like an account-takeover bug.

Post login flow can enforce additional authentication such as OTP after broker login. For I3 saml_mfa_bypass_via_binding_rule tests, a valid test requires configuring postBrokerLoginFlowAlias to a flow that enforces MFA after SAML login; otherwise successful SAML login without MFA is expected behavior, not a bypass.

Authentication sessions expire after the realm Login timeout, 30 minutes by default. SAML broker flows are session-bound; the executor must initiate the SP flow immediately before posting the SAMLResponse so InResponseTo and authentication-session state remain valid.

Authentication session sub-session limit has a numeric sentinel: authSessionsLimit=300 by default, and when the limit is reached the oldest authentication sub-session is removed as new ones are created. Multi-tab or repeated initiated SAML flows can evict older sub-sessions and break flow coherence tests.
User session count limiter has a numeric sentinel: value 0 disables the check for both realm session limit and client session limit. Never interpret 0 as literal zero allowed sessions.

For SAML client step-up tests, RequestedAuthnContext comparison supports Exact, Minimum, Maximum, or Better. The fuzzer MUST set the intended comparison explicitly; otherwise the default is Exact, which changes matching semantics and can invalidate I5 authorization-binding conclusions.
SAML client Valid Redirect URIs support wildcards only at the end of a URL pattern. Tests that rely on arbitrary redirect matching must not assume mid-string wildcards are supported.

Include AuthnStatement is enabled by default for SAML clients. Disabling it prevents clients from determining maximum session length and can create client sessions that do not expire. I2 freshness tests against downstream SAML clients must account for this by-design behavior.

Include OneTimeUse Condition on SAML clients is optional and off unless enabled. Replay protection tests against Keycloak as IdP must not assume OneTimeUse is present unless the client configuration explicitly enables it.
Assertion Lifespan on SAML clients has a sentinel: if not specified, the realm Access Token Lifespan is used. Do not assume an omitted value means no expiry.
Password policy Hashing iterations has a sentinel: value -1 means use the algorithm default iteration count, not disable hashing iterations. Defaults are algorithm-specific and nonzero.
Password policy Maximum Authentication Age has a sentinel: value 0 means the user must always re-authenticate with the current password before updating the password, not 'use default'.
WebAuthn timeout has a sentinel: value 0 means behavior depends on the authenticator implementation, not a guaranteed immediate timeout or disabled timeout.

For organization-linked IdPs with Advanced Claim to Group mapper, claim values support either exact match or regex depending on the 'Regex Claim Values' switch. For I4 multi-identity tests, if regex mode is off, wildcard-like values are exact literals and MUST NOT be used as catch-alls.

For SAML broker tests of I1 signature validation, create_provider/enable_auth_method MUST explicitly set config.validateSignature=true and config.wantAssertionsSigned=true when testing secure configurations. The documentation states Validate Signature controls whether requests/responses are expected to be digitally signed, and Want Assertions Signed controls whether the SP expects a signed Assertion. If these are omitted or left off, acceptance of attacker-signed or unsigned assertions may be by configuration rather than a vulnerability.

For insecure-default SAML signature tests, the fuzzer MUST also test the default configuration path: create_provider without config.validateSignature and without config.wantAssertionsSigned, then saml_login. The docs indicate these checks are configurable rather than always enforced, so a successful forged login under default config is evidence of insecure defaults, not of bypassing an explicitly enabled check.

Identity Provider Entity ID performs issuer validation only when configured. The documentation explicitly says: if empty, no Issuer validation is performed. For I1 saml_issuer_mismatch tests, the secure-control setup MUST set config.idpEntityId to the trusted issuer, and the attack must change the assertion Issuer. If config.idpEntityId is unset, issuer mismatch acceptance is by design due to skipped validation.

Principal Type and Principal Attribute determine which SAML assertion field becomes the external identity. For I4 principal-binding tests, the fuzzer MUST record whether the provider is configured to identify users by Subject NameID or by a SAML attribute. Testing NameID/email collision without aligning to Principal Type can misinterpret expected mapping behavior as an identity-binding flaw.

Case-sensitive username is configurable for brokered identities. If disabled, usernames from the identity provider are lower-cased before federation, while usernames in Keycloak are always lower-case. For I4 case_confusion tests, a collapse of 'Admin' and 'admin' is BY DESIGN unless case-sensitive username is enabled on the identity provider.

Trust Email changes account-linking semantics. When enabled, Keycloak trusts email addresses from the identity provider and may mark them verified on first and subsequent logins depending on sync mode. For I4 unverified_email_account_linking tests, the fuzzer MUST set trustEmail=false in the provider config; otherwise email-based linking/verification behavior can be by configuration.

First Login Flow governs whether new users are auto-created, linked, re-authenticated, or auto-linked. For I4 account-linking and collision tests, the fuzzer MUST control firstBrokerLoginFlowAlias and avoid dangerous auto-link flows unless intentionally testing them. Otherwise, automatic linking of existing accounts can be by-design flow behavior rather than a principal-binding bug.

Post login flow is the documented mechanism to enforce additional authentication after broker login. For I3 saml_mfa_bypass_via_binding_rule tests, a valid setup MUST configure a post-broker login flow that requires OTP/MFA for the brokered path. If MFA is only configured in the browser/password flow, successful SAML login without MFA may be expected because the browser flow does not continue after broker login.

Keycloak may automatically restart authentication in other browser tabs using the same authentication session/SSO context. For I3 multi-step coherence tests, the fuzzer MUST isolate browser/session state per sequence and MUST NOT interpret cross-tab auto-restart behavior as session confusion or replay acceptance.

SAML client Valid Redirect URIs support wildcards only at the end of a URL pattern. This is exact URL-pattern validation for ACS fallback behavior, not arbitrary globbing. For tests that rely on ACS or post-login redirects, the fuzzer MUST register exact URLs or suffix wildcards only where documented; malformed wildcard assumptions can cause false negatives unrelated to authorization binding.

SAML RequestedAuthnContext Comparison supports Exact, Minimum, Maximum, or Better. For step-up or MFA-related SAML tests, the fuzzer MUST account for comparison semantics; a response satisfying a stronger or equivalent context may be accepted under non-Exact modes and is not necessarily a bypass.

SAML step-up authentication returns NoAuthnContext when none of the requested contexts can be satisfied. For tests involving RequestedAuthnContext or MFA enforcement, the oracle MUST treat NoAuthnContext as the expected secure failure mode, not as a generic login failure.

Assertion Lifespan on SAML clients is a numeric lifetime parameter with sentinel semantics: if not specified, the realm Access Token Lifespan is used instead of literal zero. Never assume an omitted/empty client assertion lifespan means zero-length validity. Tests for expiry must set an explicit short value when controlling assertion validity windows.

WebAuthn/WebAuthn Passwordless policy Timeout has sentinel semantics: value 0 means behavior depends on the authenticator implementation, not strict immediate timeout or disabled validation. Never use 0 as a deterministic timeout in MFA-related broker tests.

Password policy Maximum Authentication Age has sentinel semantics: value 0 means the user must always re-authenticate before password update. It does not disable the check. Do not interpret 0 as 'use default' or 'no limit' in password-based setup flows.

Password hashing iterations has sentinel semantics: value -1 means use the algorithm default iteration count, not disable hashing or use zero iterations. Never assume -1 weakens verification; it selects the documented default for the chosen algorithm.

User session count limiter has sentinel semantics: realm max sessions 0 disables the check; client max sessions 0 disables the check. For any test environment where this authenticator is present, the fuzzer MUST know that 0 means 'disabled', not zero allowed sessions.

Authentication session sub-session limit authSessionsLimit has replacement semantics: when the limit is reached, the oldest authentication sub-session is removed after a new request. This is not a hard reject. For high-volume SAML initiation/replay tests, old sub-sessions may disappear and break correlation unexpectedly.

For I2 SAML replay tests, include a control login using a fresh valid assertion before the replayed/expired assertion attempt. Without a control, a failed SAML login cannot be distinguished from broken provider/client setup, expired authentication session state, or misconfigured bindings.

For SAML broker testing of I1 signature validation, create_provider/enable_auth_method MUST explicitly set provider config validateSignature=true and wantAssertionsSigned=true when testing secure configurations. The docs state Validate Signature controls whether requests/responses from the external IDP are expected to be digitally signed, and Want Assertions Signed controls whether the SP expects a signed Assertion. If these are left unset/off, successful forged SAMLResponse logins may be by configuration rather than a vulnerability.

For insecure-default I1 tests saml_cert_substitution and saml_post_binding_unsigned_assertion, the fuzzer MUST also run a control configuration where the SAML IdP is created with DEFAULT config and no validateSignature / wantAssertionsSigned hardening. The docs indicate signature validation and assertion-signature expectations are configurable, so acceptance under default config may reflect insecure defaults rather than bypass of an enabled check.

Identity Provider Entity ID has exact-string semantics for issuer validation. The docs state: if empty, no Issuer validation is performed. For I1 saml_issuer_mismatch tests, configure identity_provider_entity_id to the trusted IdP entity ID for the baseline; for I4 multi-identity scenarios, do NOT try to use wildcards because no wildcard/regex mode is documented for this field.

Principal Type / Principal Attribute determine which assertion field becomes the external identity. For I4 collision tests, the fuzzer MUST know whether the broker is binding on Subject NameID or a SAML attribute. If Principal Type is set to Subject NameID, changing email alone should not be expected to change identity binding; if Principal Type is set to attribute, collisions must be tested on that exact attribute instead.

Case-sensitive username is a security-relevant broker setting. By default, usernames from the identity provider are lower-cased unless case_sensitive_username is enabled. For I4 case_confusion tests, run separate baselines with case_sensitive_username=false and true; otherwise 'Admin' vs 'admin' collapsing may be by design.

Trust Email can cause account linking/import behavior that looks like an I4 bug. When trust_email is ON, brokered emails may be treated as verified and used during first-login/account-linking flows. For unverified_email_account_linking tests, the fuzzer MUST disable Trust Email or ensure the first login flow requires verification/re-authentication; otherwise email-based linking may be an intended admin-configured behavior.

First Login Flow materially changes account-linking semantics. The default first broker login flow may create a new user if unique, or prompt/link existing accounts by email or re-authentication. AutoLink/Automatically Set Existing User is explicitly documented as dangerous. For I4 account-takeover tests, record which first_login_flow_alias is configured and do not flag automatic linking as a broker flaw when an unsafe AutoLink-style flow was intentionally configured.

Post Login Flow can legitimately add MFA after broker login. For I3 saml_mfa_bypass_via_binding_rule, a valid test must compare the same user under a realm where post_login_flow_alias enforces MFA versus a path where it does not. The docs state browser flow does not continue after IdP login unless Post login flow is configured, so absence of MFA after SAML login may be by configuration rather than bypass.

Authentication sessions are flow-bound and expire. The docs state authentication sessions usually expire after 30 minutes by default (Login timeout), and SAML/OIDC browser tabs may restart authentication automatically. For I3 flow-coherence tests, the executor MUST complete the SP-initiated SAML flow and submit the forged response within the authentication-session lifetime; failures after timeout are not evidence of security enforcement.

The SAML ACS test must be SP-initiated. The docs show broker login starts at /realms/{realm}/broker/{broker-alias}/login and the ACS endpoint is /realms/{realm}/broker/{provider}/endpoint. The executor MUST initiate the SAML flow first so the forged response carries the correct InResponseTo/RelayState context; otherwise rejection is expected and not security-relevant.

Requested AuthnContext comparison supports Exact, Minimum, Maximum, and Better. For SAML step-up tests, the fuzzer MUST not assume exact-only matching. A response satisfying a stronger or otherwise acceptable context under the configured comparison mode may be valid by design.

Assertion Lifespan has no documented sentinel disable value in the provided docs; if not specified, the realm Access Token Lifespan is used. Do not assume 0 disables expiry. For I2 expiry tests on SAML clients, explicitly set assertion_lifespan when you need deterministic NotOnOrAfter behavior.

Include AuthnStatement being OFF can suppress session timing information in SAML responses. The docs state disabling it prevents clients from determining maximum session length. For I2 freshness tests that rely on AuthnStatement/SessionNotOnOrAfter, ensure include_authnstatement remains enabled.

Include OneTimeUse Condition is optional on SAML clients. For I2 saml_one_time_use_replay tests against Keycloak as SAML IdP/client behavior, the fuzzer must explicitly enable include_onetimeuse where relevant; absence of OneTimeUse in a response is by configuration, not a replay flaw.

Valid Redirect URIs for SAML clients allow wildcards only at the end of a URL pattern. This is exact/prefix-style matching, not arbitrary globbing. For I5 audience/recipient style tests involving ACS URLs, do not assume '*' matches arbitrary internal positions.

Client scopes and role scope mappings constrain what roles appear in issued tokens/assertions. By default, clients may get broad role mappings unless Full Scope Allowed is turned off. For I5 authorization-binding tests, narrow client role scope mappings first; otherwise extra roles in downstream tokens may be expected by default configuration.

Group-based authorization policy uses exact group names/paths from either a configured Groups Claim or realm configuration. Extend to Children is an explicit broadening option. For I5 group escalation tests, do not treat child-group access as a bug when Extend to Children was enabled.

Regex-based policy uses Java regular expressions on the target claim. This is not exact matching. For I5 tests involving claim constraints implemented through authorization policies, ensure the oracle accounts for regex semantics and dot/bracket JSON path extraction.

Time-based policy fields are literal times/intervals; no sentinel disable values are documented except that all conditions are ANDed. For timing tests, use explicit values and include a control request because denial may come from any unsatisfied time condition.

Hashing iterations password policy has sentinel value -1 meaning use algorithm default, not disable hashing. Never assume -1 disables the underlying check. Documented defaults: argon2=5, pbkdf2-sha512=210000, pbkdf2-sha256=600000, pbkdf2=1300000.
Maximum Authentication Age password policy uses sentinel 0 to mean always re-authenticate before password update, not 'no limit'. Never assume 0 disables the check.

User session count limiter uses sentinel 0 to disable the realm/client session-count check. If enabled with low values, legitimate new logins may be denied or oldest sessions terminated. For multi-login replay/coherence tests, control for this authenticator because failures may be due to session-limit policy rather than token/assertion validation.

Authentication session sub-session limit authSessionsLimit defaults to 300 per root authentication session; when reached, the oldest authentication sub-session is removed. For high-volume browser-flow fuzzing from one browser context, stale tabs/flows may be evicted and fail for operational reasons rather than security checks.

environment_defaults.isolation_strategy: Each test sequence MUST create its own realm using create_tenant with a unique name (e.g., valence-i1-test). Do NOT create IdPs in the master realm — use enable_auth_method in the new realm. This prevents alias conflicts (409) between concurrent sequences.
environment_defaults.idp_fields_warning: Do NOT include syncMode in enable_auth_method params — older Keycloak versions reject it as an unrecognized field. Also do NOT include caseSensitiveOriginalUsername at the top level — it belongs inside the config object.
